blocks.title: Findings
blocks.sub: Severity = impact × reach; confidence = how sure the measure is × how likely it was not meant. Ordered by severity. A low-confidence finding is a question, not a defect.
rows:
ID cards: text drawn at 9.6–12px between 620 and 765px wide, and on small phones sideways
The row is scaled by min(1, column / 757) from a 35rem column, so from 620 to 765 it is at 0.74–0.92 and the 13px rows are drawn at 9.6–12px, the names at 18–22 (sweep every 10px). 667×375 (iPhone SE sideways): 10.9px. iPad split view (639, 678, 694 wide) falls in the range. Not new: round 4 drew the same. The audit's 768 passes by 0.1px and no audit size lands in the range; sections.css:75 says «their text stays readable».
Move the deck up to a ~47rem column, or let the row overlap more before it scales; add a 680×900 size to the audit; correct the comment.

The stable scrollbar gutter takes 15px from fixed layers
book.css:63 (Oct 19) html { scrollbar-gutter: stable }. In Chromium it takes 15px off fixed boxes: the open booking window's glass stops 15px short of the right edge (1366×650), and in the box mode (?fmbox=1) .page is 1185 wide at 1200 with a strip beside it. By the spec the gutter is kept even with html overflow hidden, so Safari on a Mac with classic scrollbars (a mouse plugged in, or «Show scroll bars: Always») would show that strip next to .page's own scrollbar. Safari not available here.

medium
review: confirmed in Chromium; a second symptom found
html:not(.boxed) { scrollbar-gutter: stable }, the gutter on html.boxed .page instead, and the window's glass inset 0 on the viewport (or right: calc(100vw - 100%) undone). Check in your Safari.

The booking window's way out is a 21px target
When the calendar does not load («Календарь не загрузился»), the only way on, «Открыть запись на сайте Планёрки», is 278×21px on a 390 phone, under WCAG 2.5.8's 24px. The audit never opens the window, so it never sees it.

review: new, from the review

high
review: new, from the review; not new on the site
Under --sideways, put the notice at the right edge (the button is centred), or give the hero's text room for it.

Tiles and half-column cards drift together; the feature texts got narrower
radius/s 16 → 32 (Oct 22) against radius/m 24 → 40: ×0.67 apart on a phone, ×0.8 on a computer (×0.6 before). A tile's padding is its radius, so the feature text column went 200 → 184px at 1440×900: all four descriptions run 3 lines of 14–18 characters (3/2/3/3 before); on a 390 phone up to 5 lines of about 12.
A question: keep padding = radius on tiles (concentric corners), or cap the tiles' padding at 24 while the radius grows to 32.

Royalty titles take four lines at 320 and between 640 and 880px
3 lines at 390–600 and from 920 up; 4 lines of about 16 characters at 640–880 (the card beside its drawing at 620–730, two cards a row from 740) and at 320. decisions.json#royalty-by-shape says three lines. Round 4 had 4 lines at every width, so this is better than it was.
Write «three, four in a narrow card» in the decision, or let the title beside the drawing take more of the card (0.55 instead of 0.5).

Curves outside the one table, and one curve with two names
deck.js: power2.in / power2.inOut / power1.out for the swipe (already on Oct 19); cookies.js: its own cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1), a near-copy of move (0.25); book.css: ease-in-out for the loader dots; tokens.css copies the numbers of out and settle (CSS cannot import them: a written exception would say so). M.curve.reveal = M.curve.wave (0.5, 0, 0.5, 1), new on Oct 23. CLAUDE.md lists 7 curves; the table has 8.
Name the swipe and the drawn line in M.curve (or use move / out), reveal → wave, list the table in CLAUDE.md, and note in tokens.css that its two curves mirror M.curve.

The Telegram cap reads the window's scroll directly
nav.js initCap listens to window «scroll» and reads scrollY (lines 79–109), which CLAUDE.md forbids. Deliberate (it returns in the box mode and runs only in apps' browsers) but not recorded: telegram-cap-flicker names initCap, not this. Its colour is a literal #fff.
scroller.onScroll and y() (the same there), or the exception in decisions.json; var(--paper) for the colour.

Two dead colour tokens
--ink-40 (tokens.json still says «Footer notes»; the footer uses ink 50 since Oct 18) and --purple-light (the CTA's light purple until Oct 19) are written to tokens.gen.css and read by nothing in the styles, the HTML or the scripts. Both still sync to Figma.
Remove both (and from Figma at the next push), or re-describe them if Figma still uses them.

Two sizes off the ladder through a factor
The features' bottom padding radius/s × 1.33 (21.3 → 42.6) and the 404 page's section/pad-y × 2 (80 → 160, past the ladder's 128). Other factors land on the ladder (royalty × 1.6 = 64 → 128, legal pages × 1.5 = 60 → 120) but are roles nobody named, as the CTA's × 1.4 was until section/air-l.
feature/pad-bottom 20 → 44 and a 404 role in scale.json, so the build checks them.

After «Показать больше» the focused card can be off-screen
With 5 publications the button shows one more card and moves the focus to it with preventScroll: at 1366×650 the card ends at 667 against a 650 screen, 17px below it.

review: new, from the review
Scroll it into view (block: nearest) once it has come in, or focus without preventScroll.

medium
review: confirmed, reworded; not new
A question: if the button should come first, put it first in the HTML (row-reverse on computers).

A page step outside media.css
book.css and book.js switch the booking window at 62em (992px: Planerka's three columns); media.css and CLAUDE.md know two page steps.
Write 62em down as an own step (third party) in media.css and CLAUDE.md.

The stack's label is the heading, its titles are subheadings

The stack card's radius is derived, not on the ladder

Nothing to change; the grammar on this page names it.

blocks.title: What it changed that you might not expect
items: The audit no longer measures what phones see at its desktop sizes. html { scrollbar-gutter: stable } (book.css, Oct 19) makes headless Chromium keep 15px for a scrollbar it hides, so at 1366 and 1920 the audit lays the page out 15px narrower, as a Windows browser with a classic scrollbar would. Fine as a test, but this round's sweeps switch the gutter off to compare like with like.

The feature texts lost 8% of their width on computers (199 → 183px): 3 lines of about 16 characters.

blocks.title: The screen's size
blocks.html:
A screen counts as only as big as its height allows. Two points in scale.json: a screen 360px tall gets the sizes of a 320 screen, a 920px one the sizes of a 1440 screen. Between them it is a line, which the generator writes as

size = min(width, 2 × height − 400)

Every pixel of height a screen lacks counts as two of width. The 400 is not a choice: it falls out of the two points.

Since round 4 a role can say "by": "width" and follow the width alone (100vw): the least size of the hero's team, so a short laptop keeps a big picture.

blocks.note: Screen size for a 1440-wide window, by its height. The sizes are flat below 360 and above 920.

sections.sub: Everything that moves with the scroll is moved by the browser (sticky); the script only decides which title and drawing are shown. Updated for Oct 20: no pause, drawings at their own size, titles without blur.

items.title: The strips
items.html: Collar (the gap above a card and the bottom corners of the one it covers), cap (outside a card's top corners) and veil (the bottom edge of a card coming up) are each one hole with the card's corners, its shadow the page colour. One shape, one edge: no seams at fractional pixels. The cap's hole is 1.5px inside the card's outline, so a card's soft corner is drawn over white, never over the card before.

items.title: Wide card layout
items.html: --card-t = min(the room the old square left, 2 × padding + 12.5 title letters). The drawing's room is the rest of the card; the drawing a square of min(1.08 × room width, card height), at least 300, centred.

items.title: Follows the scroll
items.html: Offset = the scroll since it last turned, between 0 and its height, never more than the page is past the hero's bottom edge. Set as translate each scroll event (no transition).

items.title: Settles
items.html: 140ms without a scroll event: if it is part way, a glide to away (if it was last moving away, is a third of the way out and the hero is far enough up) or back. 0.42s on the arrive curve, starting at the speed it had.

items.title: Ignores the browser
items.html: For 400ms after the visible screen changes size (Safari's and the apps' bars) and while the page is pulled past its ends, the scroll does not move it (except that it always comes back over the hero); when the 400ms are over, the way the page went meanwhile decides: back if up, away if down (24px or more).

items.title: Reduce motion
items.html: Fades out after 24px down and back after 12px up, as before; never while the hero is under it.

sections.title: The grammar

items.title: Colour
items.html: Black and white at fixed strengths (ink 10/40/50/60, paper 30/55/70/86) on three near-white grounds: white page, warm sand (hero), cool mist (tools, footer). Colour comes only in solid blocks: purple for actions, one accent per subject (blue, orange, green, magenta, teal). Since Oct 20 also ink 16 and 25 (the line button) and a stronger tint (7%); ink 40 and purple-light are now set but unused.

items.title: Type
items.html: Pragmatica Ext 700 for display (hero, section headings, stack titles), Golos 400/500/600 for the rest. Line height opens as text gets smaller: 1, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3. Labels are uppercase at 0.05em.

items.title: Size
items.html: One range, 320 → 1440, in straight lines; a screen counts as only as big as its height allows. One ladder of round values for every size, type and space alike.

items.title: Shape
items.html: Three radii by card size: s (16 → 32) for tiles, m (24 → 40) for half-column cards, l (32 → 56) for full-width cards; the stack cards have their own (half the label + the padding, 42 → 65), the ID cards theirs (24 of 240, scaled with the card). A card's padding is its radius; inner corners are concentric. Exceptions: tool cards padded by their width, the CTA's centred text with generous air.

items.title: Layout
items.html: One centred column, at most 1024 wide; the stack and the CTA bleed wider by the inset. Blocks change layout at three shared column widths (S, M, L). Cards that have a shape of their own (stack, royalty) arrange themselves by it. One more page step lives outside media.css: the booking window's 62em.

items.title: Motion
items.html: Things arrive with out or settle, travel with move, leave with leave; the ID cards fade on reveal and fall on fall. Hovers 0.2s in, 0.45s out. Nothing pauses the scroll. With “reduce motion” everything is simply shown.

Their deck starts below a 35rem column, their own step: the row needs that room

items.decided: 2026-10-18; radius/m on 2026-10-18 (Tim); 16px, scaled with the card, on 2026-10-20 (Tim: smaller corners, always in proportion to the card); 24px on 2026-10-22 (Tim: 24 at most)

items.decided: Tim, 2026-10-18; body-s and body-m on 2026-10-18

items.what: The cookie notice is the same card at every screen width (276px, fixed radii 16/8, 12px text: type/note), not fluid like the rest of the page; its text uses ink 70%, its button black 5% (7% under the mouse: --tint-strong); its links underlined 1px, 3px under the baseline, in ink 20% (Tim, Oct 19; Figma has 10%), ink 30% under the mouse, as in Figma; its line height is the site's text one (1.3) instead of Figma's 1.25; after «ОК» the text stays, «ОК» turns into a drawn checkmark, the card sets off 0.15 s before the drawing ends and goes down below the screen edge while fading (0.45 s, the 'leave' curve of motion.js, as the stack titles leave)

items.why: Safari 26+ on a Mac draws its bar as glass over the page and the page shows through while it scrolls. Measured in Tim's Safari on macOS 27: no light header (solid, glass, tone strips) made the bar solid in dark mode; a page whose window does not scroll did, in light and dark mode (the Google Docs way). theme-color is ignored. Checked in Chromium: the boxed page renders pixel for pixel like the normal one at 1440×900, 390×844 and 1366×650

items.what: The privacy policy and the cookie consent are pages of the site (privacy_policy_ru.html, soglasie_cookie.html) at their old addresses. Their text is the Tilda text as it was (Tim, 2026-10-19: «keep it as is for now except formatting»); only the layout is new: headings, paragraphs, hanging list markers, one card per purpose of processing, links. Text line height 1.5 (--doc-line), not --lh-text 1.3

items.decided: Tim, 2026-10-19 (text as is); Claude, 2026-10-19 (layout, line height)

items.what: The hero has least and greatest sizes for its parts (picture, air above and below the text). On tall screens it stops growing and the first card shows more under it (390×844: 574px instead of 826); on screens shorter than about 690px it is taller than the screen rather than squeezing the picture (1366×650: 673px, the team 291px tall instead of 249, no pill of the first card on the first screen)

items.decided: Claude, 2026-10-19, from Tim's round-4 comments (hero 1–3) — to confirm

items.what: A card that has become a pill does not wait: it goes on up with the page at once and leaves the screen under the navbar, while the next card comes up to the top. The pinned pill of 2026-10-19 is gone, and its code with it (the sticky holder round each card, the last card's copy, SET.hold)
items.why: the pause felt like the page sticking; without it the stack scrolls on evenly
items.decided: Tim, 2026-10-20 — remove the sticky behaviour of a closed card pill (it was pinned for 1/5 of a screen since 2026-10-19, round-4 comment cards 5); the same day — remove the pause from the code completely

items.what: The publications show at most 4 cards; with 5 or more, a «Показать больше» pill under them shows the next 4 each time and goes away when none are left. It is --section-gap below the cards (the gap their heading had; Tim, 2026-10-20), while the heading itself has --section-air-l above the cards. It is a line button (.btn--line): no colour of its own, a 1px border, ink 70% on an ink 16% border, ink on ink 25% under the mouse (Tim, 2026-10-20), and it comes in as a block, as the hero's button does. Without scripts every card is shown and the button is not
items.why: the list can grow without the page getting longer; 4 is two full rows of the two-column grid
items.decided: Tim, 2026-10-20 — button below the cards from 5 cards; later the same day: no background, 1px border, 70%/16% → 100%/25%, coming in like the hero's button

items.what: No focus ring anywhere on the page (links, buttons, the publications the focus moves to after «Показать больше», the booking window's close button). Only the system's high-contrast modes (forced colours) keep a ring, in the system's colour. The skip link still appears when it is reached with Tab
items.why: the purple ring showed on the publication the focus moves to after «Показать больше», and on other elements; the look of the page
items.decided: Tim, 2026-10-20 — remove all design for focus states

items.what: The tools and the publications have more air than the other sections: --section-air-l (56 → 112px) above and below their content and from their headings to their cards, the same as under the CTA card (which had section-y × 1.4, the same numbers). The gap from the publications to «Показать больше» stays --section-gap
items.why: the two sections after the CTA read as a calmer, more spacious end of the page
items.decided: Tim, 2026-10-20 — top and bottom paddings 112 at most (as under the CTA card), the heading gap 112 too, the button's gap unchanged

items.what: Safari's bottom bar on iPhone takes no colour from the page: an empty block fixed over the middle of the bottom edge (.bar-guard, base.css; iOS only, 64 × 8px, takes taps), which Safari skips as see-through and then finds nothing fixed or sticky there, so the bar stays plain glass. Before, the bar turned the colour of the stack's cards and kept it after the stack (WebKit hit-tests the bottom edge through clipping and through blocks with nothing sticky in them, so the last card hidden by the stack's overflow still counted). A backdrop filter on the block (Oct 22) made the bar white instead
items.why: the green of «Финансы» stayed in the bar over the sections after the stack. WebKit LocalFrameView::fixedContainerEdges: the bar is coloured only when the hit test at the bottom edge finds a fixed or sticky container; a see-through fixed block that takes taps ends that search with nothing; a backdrop filter counts as glass of many colours (Safari then paints the bar the page colour, white)
items.decided: Tim, 2026-10-22 — «i don't want it to have any color», then «i want it to have no background» (white was not it either)

items.what: Known limit, left as it is: in Telegram's browser on iPhone, a hard fling past the end of the page makes the strip behind Telegram's buttons (the white cap, nav.js initCap) flicker for 3–5 frames (about 50–80 ms). Everywhere else the cap holds at the navbar (±1px, measured frame by frame in Tim's recordings with ?fmcap=debug, Oct 23)
items.why: the flicker is Telegram's own: in those frames it animates its top bar and moves the whole page, the fixed navbar too (debug: nav top −72, visual viewport +72); the page hears of it only after those frames are drawn, and the browser of Telegram has no setting to keep its bar still (Mini Apps have one, ordinary links do not). Already done: the bounce off in the last screen, the cap placed by the navbar's offsetTop, its scroll-driven animation 1:1 with the scroll (animation-range), its place checked 4 times a second
items.decided: Tim, 2026-10-23 — «let's do this» (record it and leave it): the top bar is white in general, a split-second flicker on a hard scroll past the end

items.what: On phones (the ID cards as a stack, a column below 35rem) the cards do not drop: they rise 80px into place one after another, the bottom card first, 0.12s apart, 0.7s each (out), turning from −4° to their angle in the stack; the whole stack fades in as one picture (0.55s, the reveal curve). In the stack the angle goes with the place, not the card: the top card straight, then 4°, then 8° (the slot carries it, so a swap turns the cards to their new places and the stack always looks the same). The row keeps the drop and each card's own angle
items.why: a stack has one card to read; the drop onto it read as a delay before anything moved, and cards fading in one over another showed each other through themselves
items.decided: Tim, 2026-10-23 — in the access-cards lab: «on mobile i want cards to move from below, one after another, no drop animation», «the top card end state to be straight and the other cards on equal angles», «on swap they should also change the angle so that the stack stays the same (0, 4, 8)», «when it's a stack there's a moment when cards overlap in their transparency. i don't want that»

items.what: The ID cards of the row start their drop tipped 20° with the top edge toward the visitor and lie flat again at an even speed by the landing (M.DROP.tip); they fade in slowly at both ends (M.curve.reveal, cubic-bezier(0.5, 0, 0.5, 1); 0.2s as before). A light from the top, 75° above the page, shades a face as the card tips or leans: brighter turned towards it, darker turned away, ×4 at most 45%, nothing lying flat (M.LIGHT). The shadow stays the site's own box-shadow, with a 0.5px hairline of the face's colour as its first layer, so no light line shows between the card's edge and its shadow
items.why: the drop reads as a card falling onto a table: it comes in at an angle and settles flat; the light makes the angle visible on the face
items.decided: Tim, 2026-10-23 — the settings of the access-cards lab (light from the top at 75°, shade 4, no gloss; tilt −20°, even, 1× the fall; fade 0.36 of the fall on 0.5, 0, 0.5, 1); «the drop shadow should be consistent with the current website»; «there's a thin white line at the bottom»

blocks.title: The independent review
blocks.sub: A separate agent that had not seen this work re-measured every finding on both builds (Chromium, swiftshader, its own scripts), tested the edge sizes and looked for what was missed. Its verdicts are on each finding above; here is what it changed.
items: F1 confirmed, range corrected: on main the deck holds to 610px, so the row starts at 620 (scale 0.740, rows 9.6px) and stays under 12px up to about 765. The audit's 768 size passes by 0.1px (12.05). The comment at sections.css:75 («their text stays readable») is no longer true. Added to the finding: 667×375 (a small phone sideways) draws them at 10.9px.

F2 confirmed in Chromium, Safari unverified, and it found a second symptom (now part of F2): the open booking window's glass stops 15px short of the right edge at 1366×650. With ?fmbox=1 the fixed .page is 1185px wide at 1200 (1200 on Oct 19), with a lighter strip beside it.
F3 confirmed: 184px of text at 1440×900 (200 on Oct 19); all four descriptions now 3 lines of 14–18 characters (3/2/3/3 before).
F4 confirmed, widened: also 4 lines at 320; Oct 19 had 4 lines at every width checked, so main is better than round 4, but the decision still overstates.
F5 confirmed, corrected: deck.js's curves were already there on Oct 19 (reveal is new); missed: tokens.css copies the numbers of out and settle, which rules.mjs had exempted (now listed).
F6, F9 confirmed, not new (the same code on Oct 19). F9 reworded: the mail answers the question; the issue is the drawn order against the Tab order.
F7, F10, F12 confirmed. F10's fix: write 62em down as an own step; the copy of --phone in JS is unavoidable and says so.

F8 adjusted: only the feature padding is off the ladder; royalty ×1.6 and doc ×1.5 land on it; the CTA's +65px is the strip's height (structure, refuted). Missed and added: 404.css section-y × 2 = 160 at 1440, past the ladder's 128.
F11 mostly refuted as a tier: it is derived (half the label + the padding) so the closed card is a pill; now a note only.

rules.mjs: one-line rules were skipped (a declaration had to start a line), integer multipliers and GSAP ease names were missed, three spacing hits were structure. All fixed in this round's version; the run on this page is the fixed one.

New, from the review: F13 (the booking window's failure link is 21px tall), F14 (the cookie notice covers the hero button at 568×320, not new), F15 (after «Показать больше» the focused card can sit 17px below the screen).

No problem at: 568×320, 844×390, 1366×650, 2560×1440, 1024×768, the browser's text at 24px (390 and 1366), reduced motion: no sideways scroll, no console errors; the ring with ?fmring=gl drew with WebGL (139–171 draws), the 2D still once. Not checked: Safari, real classic scrollbars, Planerka's calendar itself, a real GPU, the Telegram cap in an app.
